To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
social ties, social integration, and social support are beneficial for physical and psychological well being because they provide access to the mechanisms described above.

social relationships and support improve health by (1) providing social influence, (2) increasing social control, (3) enhancing purpose and meaning, (4) increasing self-esteem, (5) enhancing a sense of control, (6) increasing belonging and companionship and (7) providing emotional sustenance and instrumental aid.

the beneficial effects of social relationships and support on physical and psychological well being are due to the mechanisms of social influence, social control, purpose and meaning, self-esteem, sense and control, belonging and social companionship, and stress-buffering, and to the provision by significant others of emotional sustenance and by experientially similar individuals of active coping assistance.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the mechanisms linking social relationships to physical and mental well-being, and the ways that these mechanisms are influenced by the nature of the stressor and by the characteristics of social ties and support.
how the social world affects health, and how the health of the individual affects the social world.
how social relationships and support influence physical and psychological health and well-being and how these processes are mediated by specific mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
social support and social ties are beneficial to health and well-being because of their positive impact on the mechanisms that I have identified.
social ties and support improve health by influencing the seven mechanisms described here, with stress-buffering effects being a subset of these mechanisms.

social ties and support improve physical and mental health directly and as stress moderators through the mechanisms of social influence and social comparison, social control and social norms, role-based purpose, meaning, and self-esteem, belonging, companionship, and sense of control, and through emotional sustenance from significant others and active coping assistance from experientially similar peers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
social ties, support, and social influence are beneficial for health, and that the benefits of social support are largely mediated by the mechanisms of self-esteem, sense, and control.
social support is a complex phenomenon, with a number of potential mechanisms that may be important in understanding its effects on physical and mental health.

social relationships and social supports are important for health and well-being because they are a source of social influence and control, a source of self-esteem and self-efficacy, and a source of companionship and belonging, and that they also serve as buffers against the effects of stressors on the body and the mind.
The main takeaway from our work is that
social relationships and social ties are not monolithic, but rather complex systems of interrelated mechanisms and processes that are differentially activated by different types of social ties.
there are multiple pathways linking social relationships and support to health and that the pathways are differentially activated in different social contexts.
social relationships and social supports have multiple mechanisms that can affect health.
